thread:
devsec-bot: 🚨 secret-scanner detected possible API credential in staging logs: /svc/cc-ingest pod cc-ingest-7f8b9, file /var/log/app/stdout. snippet hashed: <redacted>
Sophie: ugh — which credential? service ingest key?
Raj: looks like the ingestion API key (cc-ingest) was printed by a debug dump in multipart handler. I pulled the raw line: `DEBUG payload: {..., \"ingest_key\": \"redwood_ingest_***\", ...}`
Emma: confirming. Repro on my side: `kubectl logs -n staging cc-ingest-7f8b9 | grep ingest_key` returns a single line around 2026-03-19T22:04:12Z
Maria: any evidence it left staging network? egress logs show no external POST with that key but we need to be sure.
Sophie: action plan: 1) rotate the key immediately 2) revoke old key 3) roll staging deployment with redacted logger 4) audit KMS and access logs 5) check customer impact
Raj: I'll create a new key in KMS now and patch the staging secret. command: `gcloud kms keys versions create --key=cc-ingest-key --location=us-central1` (we store wrapped secret in Secrets Manager)
Emma: I'll deploy a patched container that removes debug dump and adds a log scrubber. quick fix: set `LOG_SENSITIVE=false` env and redeploy.
Maria: I'll query VPC flow logs + egress proxy for any outbound traffic using that key; also checking token-usage logs in the API gateway. If anything shows external use, escalate to incidents channel and page oncall.
oncall: noted. If we find misuse, page PagerDuty token-abuse @oncall-sre and start customer-impact triage
Sophie: Raj, after you rotate please invalidate the old key in the authorization service (call `POST /admin/keys/:id/invalidate`) and post the key-id here
Raj: new key created id=key_6a9c. I've updated staging secret and redeployed cc-ingest. old key invalidation request submitted to auth-service, awaiting 200.
Emma: rollout completed, pods restarted. logs now show no ingest_key prints. added a new scrubber middleware and a unit test to prevent regression.
Maria: no external requests found referencing the old key in the last 72h. API gateway logs show only internal staging services. marking customer-impact: none so far.
Sophie: good. followups: - file a post-incident with timeline - add CI lint rule to fail if env var names match sensitive patterns in logs - require RBAC change: only the deploy pipeline's service account can read KMS keys for staging
Raj: opened INC-2026-314 in our incident tracker, attached logs and actions. assigning postmortem to Emma.
Emma: I'll write the postmortem and remediation steps: scrubber rollout to prod, CI lint, automated rotation policy for staging keys, and a dashboard for secret scanner alerts.
Sophie: also add audit logging for key creation/rotation to the compliance bucket and notify InfoSec weekly summary
devsec-bot: incident severity candidate: P3 (exposed staging credential, rotated, no external use detected). Remember to tag with `exposure:staging` and `vector:log-leak`.
Sophie: thanks team. closing the thread once Emma posts the postmortem and we push CI rule. :thumbsup:
